one_liner: Go monospace display-width and truncation library; 1.6-3.3x faster than go-runewidth v0.0.23 in its own benchmarks, zero allocations.
what_it_does: Returns the number of terminal cells a Go string, []byte or rune occupies. It sums per-grapheme-cluster widths under UAX #11 East Asian Width, with TR51 emoji, VS16 and regional-indicator flag rules. The API is displaywidth.String/Bytes/Rune, StringGraphemes/BytesGraphemes iterators that yield each cluster's width, and TruncateString/TruncateBytes with an optional tail. An Options value sets East Asian Ambiguous width and whether 7-bit or 8-bit ECMA-48 escape sequences count as zero width. It covers what go-runewidth's StringWidth/RuneWidth/Truncate do, under different names, and is not a source-compatible replacement.
how_it_is_fast: Width properties live in a generated multi-stage trie indexed directly by UTF-8 bytes, in the style of x/text/internal/triegen (trie.go: about 16 KB of values plus a 1.9 KB index). It returns a one-byte bitmap (zero-width, wide, ambiguous, VS16-eligible) without decoding runes. Runs of printable ASCII are counted by a plain byte loop that skips grapheme segmentation entirely; the changelog says 2-10x faster on ASCII than v0.7.0. Other text goes through the clipperhouse/uax29 grapheme iterator, and each cluster costs one trie lookup on its leading rune, plus an IndexByte scan for VS16. The code is generic over string and []byte and allocates nothing. The go-runewidth v0.0.23 baseline instead binary-searches interval tables per rune (up to three tables in East Asian mode), and its Truncate measures the whole string before a second cutting pass.
when_to_use: Go TUIs and CLI tables that measure or truncate many short cells per frame. lipgloss v2, charmbracelet/x/ansi (v0.11.0) and olekukonko/tablewriter (v0.10.0) already depend on it in their go.mod files.
ASCII-heavy text: 54.5 ns vs 125.5 ns for 128 bytes over five strings against go-runewidth v0.0.23 (2.3x), and 27x faster than rivo/uniseg.
Strings carrying ANSI SGR colour codes: Options.ControlSequences counts escape sequences as zero width, and TruncateString keeps trailing escapes so colours do not bleed.
Emoji-heavy output where flags, keycaps and VS16 emoji should take 2 cells, matching Ghostty, iTerm and VS Code per the author's compatibility notes.
Allocation-sensitive hot paths: String, Bytes, Rune and TruncateString without a tail report 0 allocs/op.
when_not_to_use: Before re-benchmarking against a current go-runewidth. The comparison pins v0.0.23 (2026-04-08). v0.0.24 (2026-05-29) added a precomputed East Asian width table, v0.0.28 a lazily built full-range lookup table, and v0.0.30 (2026-09-10) a rune fast path in StringWidth and Truncate. The README numbers have not been re-run, so the 2.3-3.3x East Asian gaps may have shrunk.
Code that uses go-runewidth's Wrap, FillLeft, FillRight or TruncateLeft helpers, which have no displaywidth equivalent.
Thai and similar text: a cluster's width comes from its leading rune, so Thai clusters ending in SARA AM (U+0E33) measure 1 where terminals draw 2 (issue #25, open since 2026-10-01).

Layouts that must match macOS Terminal or existing go-runewidth output exactly. Here flags and keycaps are 2 cells and VS16 forces 2, while go-runewidth gives 1, and the author notes Mac Terminal draws flags as 1.
Proportional-font text layout or shaping. It counts monospace cells only: no bidi, no line breaking, no font metrics.

integration.min_toolchain: Go 1.18 per go.mod (generics); CI tests Go 1.20-1.25 with -race. The comparison module needs Go 1.20+, because the pinned go-runewidth v0.0.23 declares go 1.20.
integration.platforms: any GOOS/GOARCH (no assembly; the published benchmark ran on darwin/arm64)
integration.thread_safety: Stateless functions over read-only generated tables, and Options is passed by value, so concurrent calls need no locking. Thread safety is not explicitly documented, and DefaultOptions is an exported mutable package variable.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: equivalent functions under different names (String vs StringWidth, Rune vs RuneWidth, TruncateString vs Truncate). East Asian Ambiguous width is not read from the locale or RUNEWIDTH_EASTASIAN as go-runewidth does at init. Results differ on flags, keycaps and VS16 sequences, and there are no Wrap or Fill helpers.

gotchas: EastAsianWidth defaults to false and is never set from the environment. Code moved from go-runewidth on a CJK locale silently changes ambiguous characters from 2 to 1 cells unless you set Options.EastAsianWidth yourself.

Invalid UTF-8 is not validated and its results are undefined; the code is fuzzed only against panics and infinite loops. ControlSequences8Bit treats C1 bytes 0x80-0x9F, which are also UTF-8 continuation bytes, as escapes, and Truncate ignores that option.

Width is taken per grapheme cluster from the leading rune, so measuring rune by rune (Rune) gives different and usually wrong totals for combining sequences, ZWJ emoji and flags. The README itself warns against it.

Unicode 17 tables are compiled in (v0.9.0). Width changes arrive with library upgrades, as with v0.5.0's VS15 change and PR #24's narrower VS16 rule in May 2026, so pin the version if column layout must stay stable.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Among the catalog's terminal-width siblings, pick displaywidth for Go code that wants grapheme-aware widths, ANSI-aware truncation and the library the Charm stack (lipgloss v2, x/ansi) and tablewriter already pull in. uniwidth's numbers are against the older go-runewidth v0.0.19 on an EPYC in CI, so the two cannot be ranked from catalog data. uwcwidth is the Python counterpart and not an alternative for Go.
verified_claims_summary: go test -bench in comparison/ on an Apple M2 (darwin/arm64), Go version unstated, numbers refreshed in the 2026-04-18 'update versions & benches' commit, against go-runewidth v0.0.23 and rivo/uniseg v0.4.7 in their default configurations. Results: about 1.7 KB of mixed test strings 6085 vs 9970 vs 19060 ns/op; the same with East Asian Ambiguous wide 6118 vs 13917 vs 19263; East Asian runes 3454 vs 11432; truncation 2495 vs 4569 (with tail) and 2456 vs 5182 (without). Reading the harness: both sides do equivalent default work, but go-runewidth's opt-in CreateLUT fast path was not enabled; its default condition follows the runner's locale; its Truncate scans the string twice; and on the emoji set (flags, VS16 emoji) the libraries return different widths. The numbers predate PR #24 (2026-05-17, VS16 rewrite, about 1% per the PR) and go-runewidth v0.0.24-v0.0.30. Record correction: go-runewidth v0.0.23's go.mod declares go 1.20; go 1.23 is its current HEAD.
status_note: Active: v0.11.0 is the latest changelog release, the last commit is 2026-05-17 and one issue is open. MIT, small and pure Go with a single dependency, and already used by lipgloss v2, charmbracelet/x/ansi and tablewriter.
